By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and law s of the  
United States of Am erica, and to eliminate Executive Orders that are no  
longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and  
any amendments thereto, are revoked:

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10872 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (25 FR 2379, Federal Register of March 22, 1960, signed March 18, 1960) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employes, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by April 17, 1960); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Pan American World Airways, Inc., or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 128 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated June 2, 1960; the board report states that the board was granted an extension of time to report to June 2, 1960. Thirty days after June 2, 1960 is July 2, 1960. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on June 2, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on July 2, 1960.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 10872
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD  
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE-  
TWEEN T H E  P A N  AMERICAN 
WORLD AIRWAYS, INC., A N D  
CERTAIN OF ITS EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Pan American World Airways, Inc.,  
a carrier, and certain of its employees  
represented by the Brotherhood of Rail­
way and Steamship Clerks, Freight Han­
dlers, Express and Station Employes, a  
labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as  
to deprive a section of the country of  
essential transportation service:
NOW,. THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the dispute  
within thirty days from the date of this  
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Pan American World Air­
ways, Inc., or by its employees, in the  
conditions out of which the dispute arose.

The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (25 FR 3567, the issue of April 26, 1960) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10875, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 22, 1960. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 22, 1960), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 130 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated June 8, 1960; the report's table of contents lists a letter of extension of the time limit. Thirty days after June 8, 1960 is July 8, 1960. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on June 8, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on July 8, 1960. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10878 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (25 FR 4575, Federal Register of May 25, 1960, signed May 23, 1960) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific Railroad Company and other carriers represented by the Western Carriers' Conference Committee (listed in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by the Switchmen's Union of North America, AFL-CIO; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by June 22, 1960); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 131 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated July 8, 1960; the report states that the parties stipulated to request an extension of time to July 15, 1960. Thirty days after July 8, 1960 is August 7, 1960. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on July 8, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on August 7, 1960.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 10878
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD
TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE CHICAGO, ROCK
ISLAND AND PACIFIC RAILROAD
COMPANY AND OTHER CARRIERS
REPRESENTED BY THE WESTERN
CARRIERS’ CONFERENCE COMMIT­
TEE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EM­
PLOYEES
WHEREAS a dispute exists between
the Chicago, Rock Island and Pacific
Railroad Company and other carriers
represented by the Western Carriers’
Conference Committee, designated in
List A- attached hereto and hereby made
a part hereof, and certain of their em­
ployees represented by the Switchmen’s
Union of North America, AFL-CIO, a
labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as to
deprive a section of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the
authority vested in me by section 10 of
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of
three members, to be appointed by me,
to investigate this dispute. No member
of the board shall be pecuniarily or
otherwise interested in any organization
of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to
the President with respect to the dispute
within thirty days from the date of this
order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this
date and for thirty days after the board
has made its report to the President, no
change, except by agreement, shall be
made by the Chicago, Rock Island and
Pacific Railroad Company or any other
carrier represented by the Western Car­
riers’ Conference Committee, or by their
employees, in the conditions out of which
the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10888 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (25 FR 9361, Federal Register of September 30, 1960, signed September 28, 1960) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between certain carriers represented by the New York Harbor Carriers' Conference Committee (listed in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by labor organizations that are members of the Railroad Marine Harbor Council, AFL-CIO (listed in attached List B); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by October 28, 1960); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 133 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated December 10, 1960; the report states that the time for filing it was extended to December 10, 1960 by the President on the consent of the parties. Thirty days after December 10, 1960 is January 9, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on December 10, 1960, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on January 9, 1961.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10953 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (26 FR 6578, Federal Register of July 22, 1961, signed July 20, 1961) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines), a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railroad Telegraphers, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by August 19, 1961); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Southern Pacific Company (Pacific Lines) or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 138 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated September 15, 1961. Thirty days after September 15, 1961 is October 15, 1961. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on September 15, 1961, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on October 15, 1961.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11101 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (28 FR 3305, Federal Register of April 5, 1963, signed April 3, 1963) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the Eastern, Western, and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees (listed in attached List A) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, and the Switchmen's Union of North America, labor organizations; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 3, 1963); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 154 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated May 13, 1963. Thirty days after May 13, 1963 is June 12, 1963. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on May 13, 1963, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on June 12, 1963.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11115 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes". This order (28 FR 6905, Federal Register of July 6, 1963, signed July 4, 1963) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between The Pullman Company, The Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific Railroad Company, the New York Central System and The Soo Line Railroad Company, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by August 3, 1963); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those four carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 155 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated November 2, 1963; the board report states that the parties agreed to extensions of time to September 19, October 19 and finally to November 2, 1963 with the approval of the President. Thirty days after November 2, 1963 is December 2, 1963. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on November 2, 1963, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on December 2, 1963.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11115
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE PULLMAN COMPANY, THE CHICAGO, ROCK ISLAND &
PACIFIC RAILROAD COMPANY, THE NEW YORK CENTRAL SYSTEM,
AND THE SOO LINE RAILROAD COMPANY AND CERTAIN OF THEIR
EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between The Pullman Company, The  
Chicago, Rock Island &  Pacific Railroad Company, the New York  
Central System and The Soo Line Railroad Company, and certain  
of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car  
Porters, a labor organization;  and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under  
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce  
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees  
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
these disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by  
The Pullman Company, the Chicago, Rock Island & Pacific Railroad  
Company, the New York Central System and The Soo Line Railroad  
Company, or by its employees, in the conditions out of which this  
dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11131 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate airline labor disputes". This order (28 FR 13485, Federal Register of December 13, 1963, signed December 11, 1963) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Braniff Airways, Inc., Continental Airlines, Inc., Eastern Air Lines, Inc., National Airlines, Inc., Northwest Airlines, Inc., and Trans World Airlines, Inc., air carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by January 10, 1964); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those six air carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by January 10, 1964) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (28 FR 13485, the issue of December 13, 1963) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11131, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated December 11, 1963. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11343 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (32 FR 6085, Federal Register of April 18, 1967, signed April 12, 1967) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between The Long Island Rail Road, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, labor organizations (three disputes); barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 12, 1967); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by The Long Island Rail Road or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 170 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated May 12, 1967. Thirty days after May 12, 1967 is June 11, 1967. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on May 12, 1967, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on June 11, 1967.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11343
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE THE DISPUTES
BETWEEN THE LONG ISLAND RAIL ROAD AND CERTAIN OF ITS
EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS, three disputes exist between The Long Island Rail  
Road, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the  
Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, International Brotherhood of  
Electrical Workers and International Association of Machinists and  
Aerospace Workers, labor organizations;  and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce  
to such a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
Section 10 of the Railway Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I hereby 
create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate  
these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or other­
wise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
these disputes within 30 days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by  
The Long Island Rail Road, or by its employees, in the conditions out  
< ? f which these disputes arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (32 FR 6085, the issue of April 18, 1967) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11343, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 12, 1967. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by May 12, 1967), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 170 (a text of the front matter of the National Mediation Board publication, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) is dated May 12, 1967. Thirty days after May 12, 1967 is June 11, 1967. Those dates come from a lead and are disclosed, not claimed as events or as the end: the clause is described only as functionally spent on May 12, 1967, the report date, with the standstill functionally spent on June 11, 1967. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11745 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order (38 FR 30429, Federal Register of November 5, 1973, signed November 1, 1973) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order (due by December 1, 1973); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by the Long Island Rail Road or by its employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by December 1, 1973) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

THE PRESIDENT 30429
E X E C U T I V E  O R D E R  11745
Creating an Em ergency Board T o  Investigate a  Dispute Between the 
L ong Island R ail R oad and Certain o f Its Employees
W HEREAS, a dispute exists between the Long Island Rail Road and 
certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad 
Signalmen, A F L -C IO , a labor organization; and
W HEREAS, this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS, this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a 
degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential transpor­
tation service:
N O W , TH E R EF O R E, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Long Island Rail Road, or by its employees, in the conditions out of 
which the dispute arose.

Identity: the held Federal Register text (38 FR 30429, the issue of November 5, 1973) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11745, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated November 1, 1973. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986 and published at 51 FR 7237 in the Federal Register of March 3, 1986. Its enacting sentence orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto", are revoked; the text states no delayed effective date and contains no saving clause, so the effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (the printed date, March 3, 1986, is the alternative reading). The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 11852 in the number column of the table (the text layer separates the number column from the subject column for this part of the table, so its subject text is not quoted). This order (40 FR 17239, Federal Register of April 18, 1975, signed April 16, 1975) created, under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference (designated in attached lists) and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railway, Airline, and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Employees, a labor organization; barred any member who is pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier; required the board to report its findings to the President within 30 days from the date of the order (due by May 16, 1975); and, as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, barred any change, except by agreement, by those carriers or by their employees in the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board made its report to the President. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C), the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts and are not the end of the order: the clause is functionally spent once the board reported and the standstill ran, and the order remained on the books until this express revocation. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by May 16, 1975) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 11852
Creating an Emergency Board T o  Investigate a Dispute Between the
Carriers Represented by the National Railway Labor Conference
and Certain o f Their Employees
A  dispute exists between the carriers represented by the National 
Railway Labor Conference designated in lists attached hereto and made 
a part hereof, and certain o f its employees represented by the Brother­
hood o f Railway, Airline, and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, 
Express and Station Employees, a labor organization; '
This dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions 
o f the Railway Labor A ct, as am ended; and
This dispute, in the judgm ent o f the National M ediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt interstate com m erce to a degree such 
as to deprive a section o f the country o f essential transportation service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in m e by 
Section 10 o f the Railway Labor A ct, as amended (45 U .S.C . 1 6 0 ), 
I hereby create a board o f three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. N o m em ber o f the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization o f railroad employees or 
any carrier.
T he board shall report its finding to the President with respect to the 
dispute within 30 days from  the date o f this order.
As provided by Section 10 o f the Railway Labor A ct, as amended, 
from  this date and for 30 days after the board has made its report to 
the President, n o change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by 
their employees, in the conditions out o f which the dispute arose. ^

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (40 FR 17239, the issue of April 18, 1975) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 11852, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the dispute described in the clause, and is dated April 16, 1975. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF (OCR for this period), and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the dossier; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order. The held-text number search for this order found no held later order that cites it other than Executive Order 12553.

Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within 30 days from the date of the order (due by May 16, 1975), and a standstill running from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. No report of the board created by this order is held among the sources cited by the dossier, so no report date and no end date of the standstill is recorded; the clause is described only as functionally spent because its report deadline (due by May 16, 1975) and statutory standstill are completed-in-time commands, with no held source fixing a date. My reading of the held texts of Executive Order 12553 and the number search of the held texts show no earlier revoking, superseding or terminating instrument for this order.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods measured here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and any attached lists follow it; the attached lists, where present, only identify carriers and labor organizations and contain no command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence and table of Executive Order 12553."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.
